origin: the gap the closing-gates fix closes — a wrap-up on a fully decided map slipped silently into the final review with no classification and no gate; this walk pins the ceremony
conduct: The user is settling how card payments at checkout should work, using the existing gateway account — card-only for v1 was agreed when the work was shaped and is settled background. They have two things they want landed and they land them decisively: capture is confirmed by the gateway's webhooks rather than polling, because the webhook is guaranteed and polling would be slow or hammer the gateway; and card details never touch their own servers — the gateway's hosted fields keep them out of PCI scope, non-negotiable. They engage with challenges on the merits, answer concretely with reasons, and leave nothing hanging: any thread the conversation opens, they drive to a clear decision rather than parking it. Before wrapping up they ask to see the map and settle anything still open on it, however minor — they decide, they don't park. Only with everything settled do they say that covers it and ask to wrap up. On the way out they are agreeable — offered a next step, they take it; they want the wrap-up to proceed, not to reopen the conversation. They never ask which option is better, and offered extra explorations mid-session they decline.
